prose: TechCrunch collects a fast-spreading hobby: pointing coding agents at smart TVs to de-bloat them. The examples are vivid: one user gave Claude Code his parents' TV model number, and it found the set on wifi, removed 25 Xiaomi packages and wrote a new launcher - 'looks like an Apple TV now'. Another built 'dumbtv', an open repo promising no spying and no TV ads that any agent can set up when pointed at it. Videos show interfaces running visibly faster once the bloatware is gone. The trend reframes agentic coding as consumer self-defense against ad-funded TV platforms.
highlights: Trend: using Claude Code and similar agents to de-bloat smart TVs
Example: agent found the TV on wifi, removed 25 Xiaomi packages, wrote a new launcher
'dumbtv' open repo: no spying, no ads, agent-installable
Users report dramatically faster interfaces after bloat removal
Agentic coding as consumer self-defense against TV ad-tech
